extracted.intended_audience: academic peer reviewers and journal editors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for academic reviewers and editors on producing sensitive, constructive, and ethical peer review reports that are actionable, respectful, and mindful of authors' wellbeing and professional norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose details of manuscripts or use privileged information from the review process for other purposes. Editors should ensure that reviews that are 'obviously disparaging or, indeed, even libellous' are not released to authors and can rescind or ask reviewers to amend comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have required expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Having the required expertise to conduct the review (COPE principle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept assignments only when you have the necessary methodological and topical expertise to provide an informed assessment. If lacking expertise, decline so editors can find suitable reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using review to gain advantage or disadvantage others
rubrics_metrics.description: Not using the process to gain an academic advantage (or to disadvantage others) (COPE principle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use reviews to promote your own agenda, obstruct competitors, or otherwise gain unfair academic benefit. Examples/anti-patterns: coercive requests to cite reviewers' work without rationale; pressuring authors to include specific citations ('MINE!! Make sure you include these...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare conflicts and self-citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear rationale and declare any recommended self-citations to the editor (use confidential comments if double-blind).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you recommend your own work, state why it is necessary and declare the relationship to the editor. Avoid recommending multiple self-citations without justification. Editors may rescind reviews that contain coercive self-citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide accurate information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure factual statements in the review are correct. Avoid speculation presented as fact. If you identify potential misconduct, state concerns cautiously and give authors an opportunity to clarify rather than making definitive accusations publicly in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be objective and constructive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the manuscript's strengths and weaknesses with evidence-based critique and actionable suggestions. Avoid ad hominem remarks or dismissive language; orient comments toward improving the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appreciate the reciprocal nature of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Appreciating the reciprocal nature of peer review (COPE principle) and the expectation that researchers contribute reviews in return for publication of their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize reviewing as part of scholarly duties; aim to complete high-quality, timely reviews. The article notes researchers may need to complete multiple reviews per one paper they submit (estimates vary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use polite language and academic kindness
rubrics_metrics.description: Do use polite language. 'Please and thank you go a long way.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame critiques politely (example phrasing: 'I wonder if the author could please check a make sure that they have followed the appropriate reporting guidelines…'). Polite wording helps maintain authors' wellbeing and promotes receptivity to feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rudeness, condescension, and disparagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't be rude or condescending in tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid disparaging statements (example anti-pattern: 'this work would be poor if it had come from an undergraduate from a lesser University, clearly this is not publishable.'). Editors should not release reviews that are obviously disparaging or libellous and may ask for amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume the best and be humble about misunderstandings
rubrics_metrics.description: Do assume the best, be humble and appreciate what you may have misunderstood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you detect a problem, consider you may be mistaken and provide authors an opportunity to clarify. This is especially important when suspecting possible research misconduct—raise concerns to the editor and allow clarification rather than making public accusations in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear, precise, actionable feedback (what, why, how)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear and precise feedback about what the authors need to change (and why and how).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give specific instructions and references (example: 'I'd be grateful if the authors could provide precise details about how they randomised (allocation concealment, sequence generation) in their study, I'd suggest looking at the following guidance for further information.'). Link to reporting guidelines where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sweeping generalisations and dismissiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't make general sweeping statements about methods, fields, or authors (e.g., dismissing whole approaches as inherently inferior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique should address specific methodological or interpretive problems rather than blanket denunciations (example anti-pattern: 'mixed methods research is simply a way of dressing up a substandard study...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight strengths even when recommending rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Do outline the strengths of the manuscript, even if you think it is inherently flawed and should not be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin or include positive acknowledgement (example phrasing: 'I congratulate the authors on the effort that they have put into this manuscript. Unfortunately, I think there are some important methodological issues that will need to be addressed, for example…'). This balances critique and supports author learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on grammar only insofar as it affects clarity; avoid insensitive remarks about language proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Do comment if poor grammar detracts from clarity. But, don't focus too much on individual typos or make insensitive comments about authors not being native English speakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out substantive language issues (e.g., inconsistent tense use: 'as you are reporting the results of a study that has been completed you should use the past tense...') and suggest revisions, but avoid mocking or excluding authors for language background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-check tone before submitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting read the review back and imagine how you would feel if you received the review you have just written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this simple sanity check to catch unnecessarily harsh phrasing or unclear requests. Revise wording to be constructive and polite where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors should manage obviously disparaging or libellous reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors have a responsibility to ensure that reviewers' reports are not released to authors when there are serious problems or if they are obviously disparaging or libellous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors can rescind reviews or ask reviewers to amend their comments. For subtler insensitivities, weigh the cost of delaying the review process against the need to ask for edits; avoid unnecessary delay but act when essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of reviewers' workload and recognise reviewing contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that peer reviewers undertake reviews on top of heavy workloads and often with no remuneration; encourage recognition and tracking (e.g., Publons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage institutions and leaders to recognise peer review as a performance metric. For reviewers: track contributions and seek recognition where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete timely, high-quality reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide timely reviews; editors depend on reviewers to complete assessments to inform publication decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is an ethical/professional expectation. The article notes difficulty in recruiting reviewers and cites estimates of how many reviews researchers should complete relative to their submissions; strive to meet deadlines and provide substantive feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of authors' mental health and the impact of insensitive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that unfair and insensitive peer review can damage authors' mental health and well‐being, particularly for early-career researchers and higher degree students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster academic kindness; avoid unnecessarily harsh language that could harm vulnerable authors. Balance critical appraisal with sensitivity to potential impacts on authors' wellbeing.
